title: A Deposit Trial
transcript: For a small bakery, an uncollected birthday cake meant hours of work and a product that was hard to sell to someone else. The owner tried asking for a modest deposit on custom orders. Customers could move the deposit to another date if they called before the bakery started decorating. Over the next two months, fewer cakes were left uncollected. The owner also noticed that several regular customers who usually ordered by phone stopped placing orders when they were sent a payment link. One of them explained that she had never paid through a link and worried she might make a mistake. The bakery began taking deposits in person as well. Phone orders from regulars picked up again, while the number of uncollected cakes stayed low.

questions.prompt: Why did the bakery introduce a deposit?
options: To cover the cost of offering home delivery
To encourage customers to order larger cakes
To reduce losses from custom cakes left uncollected
To pay suppliers earlier in the month
questions.answer: To reduce losses from custom cakes left uncollected
questions.explanation: 定制蛋糕无人领取时很难转卖，店主因此试收订金。

questions.prompt: What does the recovery in phone orders suggest about some regular customers?
options: They wanted more time to choose cake decorations.
They were willing to pay a deposit when given a familiar way to pay.
They preferred to collect cakes on weekdays.
They called mainly to ask whether their orders were ready.
questions.answer: They were willing to pay a deposit when given a familiar way to pay.
questions.explanation: 允许到店付订金后，老顾客的电话订单回升，说明付款方式影响了他们下单。
